title: Tiny and Efficient Model for the Edge Detection Generalization (TEED)
mechanism: A 58K-parameter edge detector that trains in under 30 min and gives crisp edge maps.
adaptation: A benchmark suite member for the efficiency and deployment axis on crack. Optionally an auxiliary high-resolution crack-edge branch.
min_experiment: Run TEED on crack, 3 seeds, under the benchmark protocol. Compare with house relF1@2 and FPS. No kill line: it is a reference baseline.
evidence: R: 58K params, trains on BIPED in under 30 min, adds a new generalization test set.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark member for the efficiency/deployment axis on crack-only maps; possible cheap auxiliary crack branch.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Run as suite baseline on the fixed protocol; no score claim. About 2 GPU-h.
